help.easy: Calm, happy babies. Most stay a bit calmer as they grow.
help.energy: Lively, loud and always moving. Many stay outgoing.
help.mixed: Some easy-going, some shy, some full of energy.
help.slow: Careful with new people and places at first. Many stay a bit quieter.

help.busy: Always something going on: a bit more outgoing, a bit less tidy.
help.unstable: Grown-ups often argue. Kids tend to worry more.

help.comfy: Enough for extras like trips and lessons.
help.tight: Money is often short. Kids worry a bit more.

help.city: Lots of people and new things around.

help.crowded: Big classes; teachers have little time for each kid.
help.great: Teachers who spark interest: a bit more curious and organised.

help.none: Screens whenever they like: a bit less organised, more worried.

help.big: Grandparents, aunts or uncles live with them too: lots of help.
help.one: One parent does it all: kids often help out a bit more.
help.two: Mum and dad, two mums or two dads, at home together.
help.twohomes: Parents live apart; kids go back and forth.

help.0: An only child: a little less practice at sharing.
help.1: A little one to look after: a bit kinder, a bit more organised.
help.2: A busy house full of kids: more sharing, more chatting.
help.older: A big brother or sister to look up to.

help.authoritarian: Many rules, not much warmth. Kids tend to be organised but more worried.
help.authoritative: Lots of love and clear rules. Kids tend to be a bit more organised and calmer.
help.neglectful: Parents are busy and far away. Kids tend to worry more and be less organised.

meta.intro: The same two parents could have many different kids. Here are 120 of them, growing up from 1 to 60. Genes, home, the things that happen and plain luck all shape who they become. Press play, then try changes: they add up, and you choose when they happen and how long they last. Tap a face in "All 120 kids" to follow one kid.
meta.name: Child
meta.seoDescription: 120 possible kids of the same parents, from age 1 to 60. Change the parenting style, siblings, school or screens and see how personality shifts, and how much is genes and luck.
meta.seoTitle: Parenting Simulator: Who Will Your Child Become?
